proposal.hypothesis: For the large input, the existing hierarchy launches multiple reduction kernels and a copy. A cooperative grid with an occupancy-bounded resident CTA count may replace those launches with one grid-stride reduction and a grid barrier, but per-call device/occupancy queries and cooperative-launch overhead may erase the gain. The runtime gate and baseline fallback keep unsupported launches from being assumed to work.

retained: Add a grid-stride cooperative reduction with block-local unsigned partial sums, a grid-wide synchronization point, and a single final CTA.
Bound the cooperative grid using the runtime occupancy result and device SM count; query capability and launch support for each call so setup costs remain in the full-program timing.
Avoid scratch reads/writes for a one-block grid and write zero directly for n<=0; use the original multi-kernel reduction as a fallback when cooperative launch is unavailable or rejected.
